strokes.text: The obs provider manages an OBS Studio scene collection as Terraform resources: scenes, sources, groups, filters and the placements that arrange them.
It talks to OBS over obs-websocket 5, and uses a small native OBS plugin for the group operations that obs-websocket does not expose.
Every write is read back from OBS before a resource is reported as created or changed, and the provider refuses to write while OBS is streaming or recording.
Use it to keep a stream layout in version control, review each change as a plan and rebuild a scene collection from text.
What You Can Manage
Scenes and layout: @resources/scene creates a scene, @resources/scene_item adds a placement and @resources/scene_contents declares the layer order.
Sources: @resources/source creates a source of any installed kind, while @resources/input and @resources/media_input are typed for images and media files.
Filters: @resources/filter handles any installed filter kind, and @resources/color_filter is typed for Color Correction.
Animation: @resources/move_source_filter and @resources/move_value_filter manage the filters of the Move plugin.
Groups: @resources/group, @resources/group_source, @resources/group_input and @resources/group_graph manage groups and what they hold.
Setup: @resources/plugin installs an OBS plugin, and @resources/collection_seed creates an empty scene collection.
Group resources and the two setup resources run only on macOS; see @guides/groups and @guides/filters-and-plugins.
Getting Started
Four steps take an empty scene collection to a first scene with a coloured background and a filter.
Install OBS Studio and enable the WebSocket server under Tools, WebSocket Server Settings.
Create a scene collection made for Terraform, here called My Show, and leave it selected.
Save the configuration below as `main.tf` in an empty directory.
Run the three commands that follow it.
ex:guides/getting-started
terraform init
terraform plan -out=show.tfplan
terraform apply show.tfplan
OBS shows the new scene as soon as the apply finishes, and a second plan reports no changes.
@guides/getting-started explains each block of this configuration and what to try next.
Use a scene collection made for Terraform: `obs_scene_contents` removes every placement it does not list.
Example Usage
For OBS on the same machine the provider block needs no arguments.
ex:provider
Requirements
OBS Studio with obs-websocket 5 enabled; the provider is verified against OBS 32.2.2 with obs-websocket 5.7.4.
A base canvas of 1920x1080, or another size named with `canvas_width` and `canvas_height` in the provider block.
Terraform 1.5 or later.
The native bridge plugin, only when the configuration uses group resources; see @guides/groups.
Authentication
With `password` omitted and a local `host`, the provider reads the obs-websocket port and password from the configuration file that OBS itself writes.
For OBS on another machine, set `password` from a sensitive variable and keep it out of version control.
Every resource names its `collection`, and the provider refuses to read or write while OBS has a different scene collection active.
